The available regulatory sources do not provide enough information to answer whether FDA treats a beauty bar made with sodium cocoyl isethionate, labeled as "soap," as soap under 21 CFR 720.4 or 701.3(c). The provided evidence does not define what constitutes "soap" for regulatory purposes, nor does it address the classification of syndets (synthetic detergents) or their treatment in relation to labeling as "soap."

21 CFR 720.4(a)(1) [2] requires the name and address of the person designated on the label. 
21 CFR 720.4(a)(2) [3] requires the name and address of the manufacturer or packer if different from the person designated on the label. 
 
21 CFR 720.4(a)(4) [5] requires the cosmetic product category or categories. 
21 CFR 720.4(a)(5) [6] requires the ingredients in the product. 
21 CFR 720.4(b)(1) [8] requires providing the information requested in paragraph (a). 
21 CFR 720.4(b)(3) [10] requires providing poison control centers with ingredient information and/or adequate diagnostic and therapeutic procedures for accidental ingestion or use. 
21 CFR 720.4(b)(4) [11] requires providing ingredient information to a licensed physician who requests assistance in determining if an ingredient is causing a patient's condition. 
21 CFR 720.4(c)(1)(i) [14] lists baby shampoos as a category of baby products. 
21 CFR 720.4(c)(1)(ii) [15] lists lotions, oils, powders, and creams as baby products. 
21 CFR 720.4(c)(1)(iii) [16] lists other baby products. 
21 CFR 720.4(c)(2)(i) [18] lists bath oils, tablets, and salts as bath preparations. 
21 CFR 720.4(c)(2)(ii) [19] lists bubble baths as bath preparations. 
21 CFR 720.4(c)(2)(iii) [20] lists bath capsules as bath preparations. 
21 CFR 720.4(c)(2)(iv) [21] lists other bath preparations. 
21 CFR 720.4(c)(3)(i) [23] lists eyebrow pencil as an eye makeup preparation. 
21 CFR 720.4(c)(3)(ii) [24] lists eyeliner as an eye makeup preparation.

None of the provisions in 21 CFR 720.4 address whether a product containing sodium cocoyl isethionate, labeled as "soap," is classified as soap under FDA regulations. The listed categories (e.g., baby products, bath preparations) do not include or define syndet-based beauty bars labeled as soap. Therefore, the regulatory text does not establish that such a product is treated as soap.
